G.evidence: No mention of grace or gravity.

M.evidence: No mention of meaning or mass-force.

E.evidence: Energy is discussed as derivative from information: 'Matter and energy are derivative; distinguishability (information) is fundamental.' Also Landauer's principle: 'Erasing one bit of information dissipates at least kT ln(2) joules of energy.'

S.evidence: No mention of strong force or love.

T.evidence: Thermodynamics is central: Landauer's principle, entropy production, 'Information erasure has irreducible physical cost.' Also ISO-003 (Entropy/Sin) is referenced.

K.evidence: Information primacy is the core thesis: 'Information as ontologically primitive — Wheeler's It from Bit thesis.' Knowledge/Logos is explicitly mapped: 'In the beginning was the Word (Logos) — rational, structuring information precedes and generates all material reality.'

R.evidence: No mention of relativity or relationship.

Q.evidence: Quantum mechanics is foundational: 'Quantum information theory: The quantum state |ψ⟩ is the most complete description of a system.' Zeilinger's principle, superposition, collapse, and ISO-011 (Superposition/Collapse) are referenced.

F.evidence: No mention of weak force or sin-conservation.

C.evidence: Coherence is implied through the Logos as integrating principle: 'in him all things hold together' (Colossians 1:17). The Christ operator is referenced via the Logos as second person of the Trinity, but not explicitly as C.

physics_process_detection.specific_process: information-theoretic generation of physical reality (It from Bit), Landauer erasure, quantum information processing
physics_process_detection.equation_present: R = f(I) (physical reality emerges from informational substrate); M = f(L) (material reality emerges from Logos); Landauer's principle: E ≥ kT ln(2) per bit erased

theological_structure.trinity_structure: Logos as second person of the Trinity (ISO-001 referenced); Father as source; Spirit not explicitly mentioned but implied through creation by speech act

father_aspect.evidence: God as source of the Logos: 'the Logos was with God, and the Logos was God.'

son_aspect.evidence: Logos identified with Jesus Christ: 'John takes this loaded term and identifies it with a specific person (Jesus Christ).'

spirit_aspect.evidence: No explicit mention of the Holy Spirit.
